newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU justice chief rejects prostitution legalisation.
newsitem.headline: EU justice chief rejects prostitution legalisation.

text.p: The European Union commissioner leading the bloc's fight against illegal trafficking of women for sex rejected criticism on Friday that her approach was too narrow because it did not call for legalising prostitution.

Justice Commissioner Anita Gradin said she was surprised by comments made by Nel van Dijk, a leading European Parliament deputy who said it would be impossible to end illegal trade in flesh without legalising voluntary prostitution.
"I don't understand that you have to link the question of legalising prostitution with trafficking in women because in most cases prostitution is legal," Gradin told Reuters.
"In most countries it's not prostitution that's criminalised, its those that are using it," she said.

Van Dijk, the Dutch chairwoman of the parliament's Women's Rights Committee, told Reuters in a recent interview that it was "important to ensure the criminal part of prostitution is abolished and brought under control".
But, she added, there was no need to stamp out prostitution altogether. "Why would you want to?" she said.
Gradin, the Swede who put the issue on the EU's agenda at a major conference in Vienna last year, said that she could not understand why the two issues should be linked.

She is seeking an EU-wide solution to help women tempted from eastern Europe to the promise of better lives in the West as dancers, hostesses and hairdressers, only to be forced into prostitution on arrival.

But Van Dijk said Gradin's approach was too narrow. "The Commissioner does not accept calling prostitution work -- because it should be banned, because it is bad for women, because it is humilitating."

Adopting such a "moral and clean hands approach" had the effect of sweeping all prostitution under the carpet, ruling out any legal control over the business and giving more power to the illegal pimps."

Van Dijk said that women in legal brothels in Amsterdam earned good wages, paid taxes, got social security and could leave when they liked, while illegal prostitutes were trapped in the clutches of often violent pimps because they had no identity papers or wages.
